description: A November 2019 report from the Mineta Transportation Institute by Brian Michael Jenkins and Bruce Butterworth that expands and updates the database behind their May 2018 study of vehicle ramming as a terrorist threat. The database now tallies 184 vehicle ramming attacks since 1963 (the executive summary says 1970 in one place), of which 128 have occurred since January 1, 2014, with 481 fatalities. The report presents long-term trends in attacks and lethality, counts by country and region, attacker categories (mentally unstable individuals account for 91 of the 184 attacks and jihadists for 19), target categories, lethality enhancers, planning, how vehicles were acquired, and a separate 2014 to 2019 analysis. It closes with countermeasures, including the role of rented vehicles and ways to protect pedestrians, and lists recent publications. Coverage: incidents worldwide, with Europe and the United States accounting for more than half of the recent attacks. Format and access: a free 65-page PDF; the incident list itself is summarised in tables, not released as a file. The authors note that including or excluding a case needs judgement. Caveats: the tally ends in September 2019. Useful for threat scenarios in public space security and hostile vehicle mitigation planning; related records are not yet linked.
